answer.text: Whether powers are universally limited to one use per encounter.
answer.answer: No. Powers are normally usable once per relevant context, unless their text specifies otherwise.

answer.text: How Hate illustrates a contextual limit.
answer.answer: Hate’s Rage is tied to the start of its own turn; it is not a blanket once-per-encounter limit independent of timing/context.

answer.text: How Vulch illustrates a contextual limit.
answer.answer: Vulch’s Salvage applies whenever another player discards an artifact, so it can trigger for each eligible discard event rather than only once per encounter.

clauses.clause: Are alien powers universally limited to one use per encounter?
clauses.result: No. Powers are normally usable once per relevant context unless their text says otherwise.

clauses.clause: What usage rule applies absent specific text, and how do Hate and Vulch illustrate explicit/context-based limits?
clauses.result: Use the power at most once per relevant context. Hate’s Rage is tied to the start of its own turn; Vulch’s Salvage is triggered whenever another player discards an artifact, with each qualifying discard as its context.

literal_question.question: Amoeba legally invokes ooze to move all twenty ships, which will reduce its home colonies below the power-maintenance threshold. Does loss of its power interrupt the move, or when does the loss occur?

required_facts: All twenty chosen ships move as one complete effect.
Amoeba loses its power after the move has completed, not partway through it.
contextual_background: Amoeba began with its power active and this is a legal invocation; ordinary ooze eligibility is background, not scored.

clauses: Whether Amoeba’s all-twenty-ship Ooze is interrupted by falling below the home-colony power threshold.
When the power loss occurs.

answer.text: Whether Amoeba’s all-twenty-ship Ooze is interrupted by falling below the home-colony power threshold.
answer.answer: No. Amoeba moves all chosen ships simultaneously, so it can complete the entire twenty-ship move before losing power.

answer.text: When the power loss occurs.
answer.answer: Power is lost once the move leaves Amoeba with fewer than three home colonies; the loss does not interrupt the simultaneous movement.

clauses.clause: Does losing Amoeba’s power interrupt a legal ooze moving all twenty ships, or when does the loss occur?
clauses.result: No. Amoeba moves all chosen ships simultaneously; it can ooze all twenty before losing its power for stripping home colonies.
